title: Piyush Goyal Invokes Ambedkar, Calls Opposition Street Protests the 'Grammar of Anarchy'
excerpt: The commerce minister argues the courts are already handling the SIR and Form 6 dispute, so the Delhi marches demanding the election chief's dismissal have no constitutional excuse.
body:
• Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on Tuesday quoted B.R. Ambedkar to call the Opposition's street protests over voter-list revision the "grammar of anarchy," NDTV reported.
  • Goyal said the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of Bihar's Special Intensive Revision in May 2026 and is already examining the Form 6 question.
  • The protests, running since October 10, demand the dismissal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR and Form 6 dispute.
  • The Opposition has taken its case to the Supreme Court as well, filing a plea against the CEC after its march — the court route Goyal says should replace the street.

Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal joined the government's attack on the Opposition's Delhi protests on Tuesday, asking why parties that claim to respect the Constitution were taking to the streets when courts and constitutional methods were available to them. Quoting B.R. Ambedkar, Goyal said abandoning constitutional methods when they exist is the grammar of anarchy, according to NDTV's report of his remarks.

"When constitutional methods are available, abandoning them is the grammar of anarchy."

— B.R. Ambedkar, quoted by Piyush Goyal, via NDTV

The argument: the courts are already seized of it

Goyal's case rested on process. The Supreme Court, he said, upheld the constitutional validity of Bihar's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in May 2026. On Form 6 — the form used to add new voters, and the other flashpoint in the dispute — he said the judicial process is already in progress and the court will direct corrections if any are needed. If the Opposition truly respects the Constitution, he asked, why take to the streets?

What the protests are about

Delhi has seen large protests since October 10, after the Opposition seized on a report that the voter-list revision had split the Election Commission itself, with two commissioners recording reservations on SIR and Form 6 in writing as many as 14 times, NDTV reported. The Opposition is demanding the dismissal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi and thousands of supporters have been detained multiple times during the demonstrations, which have brought extensive road closures, metro shutdowns and barricades to the capital. Our earlier coverage tracked the march in the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court.

The other side

Opposition leaders argue the street and the courtroom are complements, not alternatives: they marched to the Supreme Court and filed a plea against the CEC seeking an interim stay on SIR, as live coverage of the October 12 march reported. Other BJP leaders have used similar language in recent days — Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Congress of creating anarchy and questioning constitutional institutions, and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav urged the party to introspect on its defeats instead. The Supreme Court has taken note of the detentions and the authorities' handling of the protests, and its next hearing will test Goyal's claim that the judicial route is working.

What to watch

The court's examination of Form 6 is now the substantive battleground. A direction on corrections would vindicate the government's process argument; a stay would vindicate the Opposition's decision to escalate. Either way, the Ambedkar line Goyal deployed on Tuesday is likely to be quoted back by both sides.
